data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental in June? You're choosing one of the best months for a charter on the Costa del Sol — warm sunshine, calm seas, and long daylight hours. But for some, the worry of seasickness can dampen the excitement. This guide covers what to expect from sea conditions in June, practical prevention tips, and how our fleet and skippers ensure a comfortable experience. Whether you're booking a boat rental in Marbella for a family outing or a group celebration, preparation is key.

Why June Is Prime Time for Marbella Boat Rentals

June offers the sweet spot of Mediterranean weather: average air temperatures of 25-30°C, sea temperatures around 21-23°C, and over 10 hours of sunshine daily. The water is warm enough for swimming, and the beaches from Puerto Banús to Cabopino are inviting. Sea conditions are typically calm, with wave heights below 0.5m, making it ideal for those new to boating. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, but our skippers know the local microclimates and can adjust the route to sheltered spots like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés.

Seasickness Prevention: What Works

Seasickness affects about one in three people, but it's manageable. Start prevention the night before: avoid heavy meals and alcohol. On the day, eat a light breakfast (bananas and crackers are good), stay hydrated, and take motion sickness medication like Dramamine or Stugeron 30-60 minutes before departure. Ginger candies, acupressure wristbands, and focusing on the horizon also help. Our skippers are trained to navigate for comfort, avoiding choppy areas. For those particularly worried, we recommend booking a larger vessel like the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m), which offer more stability.

Our Fleet: Stable Options for Every Group

We operate from Puerto Banús with a diverse fleet. For seasickness-prone guests, larger boats with deeper hulls or flybridges provide a smoother ride. The Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax, €749/2h) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax, €749/2h) are popular for their balance of size and affordability. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, €4,719 minimum 4h) includes a free jet ski and offers exceptional stability. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and refreshments — so you can focus on enjoying the day.

What’s Included in Every Charter

Every Marbella boat rental from us includes: a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. The skipper handles navigation and docking, so you can relax. If you're concerned about seasickness, let us know when booking — we can recommend the best vessel and route for your group.

Best Routes for Smooth Sailing in June

Our skippers often recommend heading east toward Cabopino or west toward Estepona for calm waters. The coastline between Puerto Banús and Cala del Faro is sheltered from the prevailing winds. For a longer trip, Sotogrande offers a protected marina and lunch spots. Morning departures (10:00-14:00) generally have the flattest seas, while sunset charters (18:00-21:00) offer stunning views of La Concha with minimal swell. If conditions change, the skipper will adapt — your comfort is the priority.

Frequently Asked Questions

Yes, June is excellent. Sea conditions are generally calm, with minimal swell and light winds. Air temperatures range from 25-30°C, and you get over 10 hours of sunshine. It's less crowded than July and August, making it ideal for a relaxed charter.

Start prevention the night before: avoid heavy meals and alcohol. On the day, eat a light breakfast, stay hydrated, and take motion sickness medication like Dramamine 30-60 minutes before departure. Ginger candies and acupressure bands also help. Our skippers can recommend the smoothest route.

Larger boats with stabilizers, like the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Ferretti 94 (29m), offer the smoothest ride. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) also provides a stable platform. For smaller groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) is well-balanced. All our skippers are experienced in handling conditions.
